what.text: L-carnitine (levocarnitine) is a natural substance that moves long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria, where they are burned for energy. FDA’s Carnitor label describes it as required in mammalian energy metabolism.

src.label: Carnitor (levocarnitine) Injection label, DailyMed

research.text: Most L-carnitine weight studies used supplements, not injections. Injection studies we found were small or in kidney dialysis patients, not healthy people seeking energy or fat loss.

research.title: IV L-carnitine during a 5-day modified fast

facts.v: Randomized, single-blind, placebo (saline)-controlled pilot; L-carnitine by IV
30 adults with metabolic syndrome (15 per group), all on a 5-day modified fast
Weight, waist, blood pressure, liver and metabolic blood tests, hunger and fatigue scores

research.found: The L-carnitine group lost more weight (4.6 vs 3.2 kg) and waist, and fatigue scores fell, while they rose in the saline group. This was a 7-day fasting study in 30 people; it did not test injections outside a fast.

src.label: Zhang JJ, et al. Nutr J, 2014 (PubMed)

research.title: IV L-carnitine after dialysis (exercise and quality of life)

facts.v: Two randomized, placebo-controlled trials; IV L-carnitine after each dialysis session, three times a week
People with end-stage kidney disease on hemodialysis: 56 in study A, 127 in study B
Peak exercise capacity (VO2max, main measure) and a kidney disease quality-of-life questionnaire

research.found: Blood carnitine rose, but VO2max did not change in either study on the main analysis. The fatigue part of the questionnaire improved vs placebo at 12 and 24 weeks; the total score did not. No drug-related side effects were identified.

src.label: Brass EP, et al. Am J Kidney Dis, 2001 (PubMed)

research.title: L-carnitine supplementation and body weight

facts.v: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of L-carnitine supplementation, searched to January 2019
Body weight, BMI, fat mass, waist, body fat percent

research.found: Compared with control, body weight was 1.21 kg lower, BMI 0.24 lower and fat mass 2.08 kg lower; waist and body fat percent did not change. Only the weight effect held in high-quality trials. The abstract describes oral intake and does not report injection trials.

us.text: Levocarnitine is FDA approved as Carnitor (tablets 1985, oral solution 1986, injection 1992) and as generics, for carnitine deficiency. Using it for energy or weight loss is off-label.

FDA’s Drugs@FDA data lists Carnitor tablets (NDA 018948, original approval December 1985), Carnitor oral solution (NDA 019257, April 1986) and Carnitor injection (NDA 020182, December 1992), plus generic levocarnitine tablets, solutions and injections.

items.text: Primary systemic carnitine deficiency, and secondary carnitine deficiency from inborn errors of metabolism.

items.text: Inborn errors of metabolism that cause secondary carnitine deficiency, and preventing and treating carnitine deficiency in people with end-stage kidney disease on dialysis. The label says it is for intravenous use only.

items.text: Carnitor raises carnitine levels, but its effects on the signs and symptoms of deficiency and on clinical outcomes in dialysis patients “have not been determined.”

world.lead: Levocarnitine is an approved medicine for carnitine deficiency in the US (Carnitor) and in Canada (Carnitor). EMA’s central list has no levocarnitine product. The UK, national EU status and Australia were not confirmed.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Carnitor and generics) for carnitine deficiency. Prescription-only. Energy or weight-loss use is off-label; compounded blends are not approved.
Approved medicine: Carnitor (DIN 02144336, by mouth), marketed since 1995.

after.title: Sport
after.text: L-carnitine is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Separately, the lists' method M2.2 bans intravenous infusions or injections of more than 100 mL per 12-hour period, except in hospital treatment, surgery or clinical tests.

side.text: The Carnitor labels list serious allergic reactions and seizures, as well as stomach upset and body odor.

items.text: Anaphylaxis, throat swelling and bronchospasm after IV use, mostly in dialysis patients, some within minutes. Rash, hives and facial swelling with oral use.

surprises: The FDA-approved Carnitor injection is labelled for intravenous use only, while compounded lipotropic blends with L-carnitine are sold as shots for energy and fat loss.
Even for the approved dialysis use, the Carnitor label says effects on symptoms and clinical outcomes have not been determined.
